summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent installs a WebSocket-driven remote shell and filesystem controller
details: On startup, the package opens an outbound WebSocket connection to a configurable server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL/config to any remote endpoint) and dispatches server-originated messages to handlers that give the remote peer full control over the host. `terminal_create` spawns a shell PTY and `terminal_input` writes server-supplied bytes directly into that PTY (term.pty.write(msg.data)); additional handlers implement arbitrary filesystem read/write/delete/move (`write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`) and git operations (`git_push`). An `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to run `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restart itself via a generated upgrade.sh executed detached under bash, letting the remote peer force reinstallation on demand. On startup the agent also `git clone`s https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git (unpinned default branch) into ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/yeaft-skills-dev, subsequently `git pull --ff-only`s it, copies the tree into the Claude plugin cache, and enables the plugin in ~/.claude/settings.json — mutable HEAD becomes trusted plugin code executed by Claude CLI on the host. service/linux.js modifies PATH to prepend ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin. The remote-shell/filesystem/git surface fires whenever the agent runs and connects to its configured server, granting the operator of that server RCE and full filesystem control on the host running the agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
